You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_276f8e5f_project_boundary_dominoes_toward_opposite_edge', kind='memory', title='ARC task-276f8e5f: connect boundary-bar offsets to markers and opposite edge', content="For task-276f8e5f with horizontal boundary bars (top and bottom rows), use each bar as a column segment. The sparse marker pixels lie between a boundary bar and the grid interior on the same columns as that bar. For each marker, draw its marker-color ray from the adjacent boundary bar toward the marker, stopping just before it; recolor the original marker to 4. Also map each marker's column offset within its adjacent bar to the corresponding offset within the opposite bar, and project that opposite-bar cell through the interior to the far boundary using the marker color. Preserve both bars, all cells beyond each marker on its local ray, and all unrelated cells. When the bars occupy different columns, offsets are left-to-right within the bar segments (e.g. offset 0 in top segment maps to offset 0 in bottom segment). This describes both the marker-local rays and the full rays projected from the opposite bar; do not draw only a ray from one arbitrary endpoint.

Accepted demo (12x8): background 0; top bar color 6 at row 0, cols 5–7; bottom bar at row 11, cols 0–2; marker 1 at (2,7). Draw 1 at (1,7), change marker (2,7) to 4, and project the matching offset 2 from the bottom bar upward in col 2, rows 0–10. Preserve bars/background.

Accepted test (14x11): background 7; top bar color 2 at row 0, cols 3–5; bottom bar at row 13, cols 0–2; marker 3s at (3,4), (7,3), (7,5). Local rays from the top bar fill (1–2, col 4), (1–6, col 3), and (1–6, col 5); replace each original marker with 4. Project their offsets 1,0,2 from the bottom bar as full 3 rays in cols 1,0,2, rows 0–12. Preserve both bars and all other cells. This submission was accepted.

Earlier confirmed examples following the same rule: (a) background 7, top 8-bar at cols 14–15 and bottom 8-bar at cols 9–10, marker 3 at row 3 col 9: project offset 0 from the top bar down col 14 to the bottom edge; draw upward from bottom-bar col 9 to just before the marker, then change marker to 4. (b) background 9, top 0-bar cols 3–4 and bottom 0-bar cols 16–17, marker 1 at row 5 col 3: project offset 0 from bottom bar upward in col 16 to the top edge; draw downward from top-bar col 3 to just before the marker; change marker to 4. Marker recolor is always 4, not input-color+1.

Rotated cases with vertical boundary bars are handled by swapping rows/columns: rays run horizontally, and marker row offsets map between opposite edge segments. A related accepted example: background 5; right-edge color-8 bar in rows 0–4, left-edge bar rows 10–14; sparse 1 markers at (10,5),(12,3),(13,6),(14,4). Local rays go rightward from each marker toward the adjacent left bar; markers become 4. Matching row offsets 0,2,3,4 are projected across the opposite right-side segment (rows 0,2,3,4), leaving row 1 unchanged. Preserve bars and unrelated cells.

Accepted test (25x6, background 6, bar/marker color setup): top-right boundary bar color 3 at rows 0–3, col 5; opposite bottom-left bar color 3 at rows 19–22, col 0; color-7 markers at (20,3),(21,4),(22,2). Project marker offsets 1,2,3 from the lower bar segment to top rows 1,2,3: fill columns 0–4 with 7 on each of rows 1–3, preserving col 5 bar. Extend each bottom marker leftward toward col 0: on row 20 fill cols 1–2 with 7 and recolor marker col 3 to 4; on row 21 fill cols 1–3 with 7 and recolor col 4 to 4; on row 22 fill col 1 with 7 and recolor col 2 to 4. Preserve all bars and other background cells. This instance was accepted on the first submission.

Important endpoint nuance confirmed on a 29x8 test: projected rays from the opposite boundary segment include the far grid edge, even in cells outside that edge's bar (e.g. a top bar at row 0 projects down through row 28 inclusive; preserve only the actual bar cells). A first answer that stopped projected rows at 27 was rejected; extending the two projected columns into row 28 fixed it. In contrast, local rays from the adjacent bar stop immediately before the marker, the marker becomes 4, and cells beyond the marker toward the far side stay unchanged. This was confirmed by demos where projected rays fill the opposite boundary row/column outside its bar, while local rays only fill the gap between marker and adjacent bar.
